originalTitle: Jeffrey Gundlach says the bond market is telling Warsh the Fed has to start acting on inflation
summary: Gundlach said the divergent moves across the Treasury curve showed investors' skepticism that the Fed will ultimately follow through.
content:
DoubleLine Capital CEO Jeffrey Gundlach said the Treasury market is signaling that the Federal Reserve will need to do more than talk tough if policymakers are serious about reaching their 2% inflation target.

"If you really want to get to 2%, I think you have to raise interest rates," Gundlach said on CNBC's "Closing Bell" Wednesday after the Fed's latest policy decision. "I think getting 2% is going to take a long time. We might not get there over the course of the next couple of years."

The Fed left its benchmark interest rate unchanged at a range of 3.5% to 3.75%, a decision that was widely expected. The move was not approved unanimously, however, with three policy members dissenting in favor of raising rates by a quarter percentage point.

Gundlach said the divergent moves across the Treasury curve following the announcement showed investors' skepticism that the Fed will ultimately follow through.

"The two-year Treasury rallied today because it thinks the Fed is taking its time," he said. "And the long bond yield went up significantly after the press conference, because the bond market vigilantes are saying, 'If you really want us to believe your rhetoric, you've got to start acting.'"

The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield rose more than 7 basis points to 4.681%, while the 30-year bond yield surged to 5.213% for its highest level since 2007. Meanwhile, the policy-sensitive two-year Treasury yield fell 3 basis points to 4.244%.

The long end is generally tied to expectations for inflation and deficits, while the short end is closely related to interest-rate expectations in the shorter run.

Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh stressed that the Fed will take necessary steps to meet its 2% inflation goal.

"I understand the desire for rolling forecasts and commentary from this committee, but for our part, we need to observe market reaction to developments direct and unfiltered," Warsh said. "I want to stress, of course, that decisions by this committee matter a great deal, and where necessary and appropriate, we will not hesitate to act."
chineseTitle: 杰弗里·冈拉克表示，债券市场正在告诉沃什，美联储必须开始对通胀采取行动
chineseSummary: 冈拉克表示，国债曲线上的不同走势表明投资者对美联储最终会采取行动持怀疑态度。
chineseContent:
DoubleLine Capital首席执行官杰弗里·冈拉克(Jeffrey Gundlach)表示，国债市场正在发出信号，如果政策制定者认真实现2%的通胀目标，美联储需要采取的不仅仅是强硬言论。

周三，在美联储做出最新政策决定后，冈拉克在 CNBC 的“收盘钟”节目中表示：“如果你真的想达到 2%，我认为你必须加息。” “我认为达到 2% 需要很长时间。我们可能在未来几年内无法实现这一目标。”

美联储将基准利率维持在 3.5% 至 3.75% 的区间不变，这一决定符合市场普遍预期。然而，此举并未获得一致批准，三名政策成员反对加息四分之一个百分点。

冈拉克表示，这一消息公布​​后，国债曲线走势出现分歧，这表明投资者对美联储最终是否会跟进表示怀疑。

“两年期国债今天上涨，因为它认为美联储正在慢慢来，”他表示。 “新闻发布会后，长期债券收益率大幅上升，因为债券市场维护者说，‘如果你真的想让我们相信你的说辞，你就必须开始采取行动。’”

基准10年期国债收益率上涨逾7个基点至4.681%，30年期国债收益率飙升至5.213%，创2007年以来最高水平。同时，政策敏感的两年期国债收益率下跌3个基点至4.244%。

长期端通常与通胀和赤字预期相关，而短期端则与短期利率预期密切相关。

美联储主席凯文·沃什强调，美联储将采取必要措施实现2%的通胀目标。

沃什说：“我理解该委员会对滚动预测和评论的渴望，但就我们而言，我们需要直接且未经过滤地观察市场对事态发展的反应。” “当然，我想强调的是，该委员会的决定非常重要，在必要和适当的情况下，我们将毫不犹豫地采取行动。”
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
